annotation.title_clean: DRAFT Compromise Amendments on the Draft Report: Proposal for a regulation on harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
annotation.title_en: DRAFT Compromise Amendments on the Draft Report: Proposal for a regulation on harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament, Committee on the Internal Market and Consumer Protection (IMCO) and Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE)
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament IMCO/LIBE joint committee draft compromise amendments (May 2023) to the Commission's proposed AI Act. They cover notified bodies and conformity assessment, high-risk obligations, AI literacy, delegated acts and environmental impact. It is a general risk-based AI regulation text with no robot-specific provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Member States designate notifying authorities to assess, designate and monitor conformity assessment bodies (Arts 30-33).
Notified bodies must be independent and meet cybersecurity requirements, with a 12-month bar on other services to the provider.
Commission to review Article 5, Article 52 and Annex III at least yearly, consulting the AI Office.
Providers and deployers must ensure sufficient AI literacy of their staff.
Commission to develop a methodology to measure the environmental impact of AI systems.
